title: Hot Jupiters around young stars
text: We report radial velocity measurements of twelve young solar-type stars in a nearby open cluster. Three show periodic signals consistent with giant planets on orbits shorter than five days. Stellar activity and spots mimic such signals, so we compare the velocity period with the photometric rotation period of each star and reject one candidate whose signal tracks the spot cycle.

title: Dust lanes in edge-on spiral galaxies
text: Near-infrared imaging of forty edge-on spiral galaxies reveals that dust lanes thin sharply in galaxies with rotation velocities below about one hundred kilometres per second. We model the vertical scale height of the dust and the stellar disc together and argue that turbulence in low-mass discs lifts dust above the midplane, where it no longer forms a coherent lane.

title: A transiting super-Earth in the habitable zone
text: Space photometry recorded four transits of a planet 1.6 times the radius of Earth crossing a quiet M dwarf every thirty-one days. The orbit places the planet inside the habitable zone of its host star. Follow-up spectroscopy constrains the mass to under eight Earth masses, and the transit depth is stable across infrared and optical bands, ruling out a blended eclipsing binary.

title: Timing a millisecond pulsar binary
text: Eight years of radio timing of a millisecond pulsar in a binary orbit with a white dwarf companion measure the Shapiro delay to high precision. The delay yields a pulsar mass of 1.97 solar masses, one of the heaviest neutron stars known, which excludes equations of state for dense nuclear matter that cannot support stars this massive.

title: Redshift survey of luminous red galaxies
text: We measure the clustering of three hundred thousand luminous red galaxies between redshift 0.2 and 0.7. The correlation function shows the baryon acoustic peak near one hundred megaparsecs, a standard ruler imprinted by sound waves in the early universe. Comparing its apparent size at two redshifts constrains the expansion history and the equation of state of dark energy.

title: Supernova light curves as distance indicators
text: Type Ia supernovae brighten and fade over weeks, and brighter explosions decline more slowly. Calibrating this relation with supernovae in galaxies of known distance, we fit light curves for ninety distant events. Their luminosity distances lie beyond what a decelerating universe predicts, consistent with an accelerating cosmic expansion.

title: Gas inflow onto a supermassive black hole
text: Millimetre interferometry of the nucleus of a nearby Seyfert galaxy resolves molecular gas spiralling toward the central black hole. Velocity maps show non-circular motions along a nuclear bar that remove angular momentum from the gas. The implied inflow rate is sufficient to sustain the observed X-ray luminosity of the accretion disc for several million years.

title: The cosmic microwave background power spectrum
text: Temperature anisotropies in the cosmic microwave background, measured across the full sky, show a sequence of acoustic peaks in angular power. The position of the first peak indicates a spatially flat universe, and the relative heights of later peaks fix the baryon and dark matter densities. A six-parameter cosmological model fits the spectrum within its uncertainties.

title: Spectroscopy of a comet's coma
text: High-resolution optical spectra of a long-period comet near perihelion show emission from cyanogen, diatomic carbon and sodium in the coma. The sodium tail extends a million kilometres from the nucleus, pushed outward by solar radiation pressure. Production rates of each species rose steeply as the comet approached the Sun, tracking sublimation of surface ices.

title: Stellar streams in the galactic halo
text: Proper motions from an astrometric satellite reveal thin stellar streams wrapping the Milky Way halo, the debris of disrupted globular clusters and dwarf galaxies. Gaps and kinks along one stream suggest encounters with dark matter subhalos. Modelling the stream orbit constrains the shape of the galactic gravitational potential out to fifty kiloparsecs.

title: Brown dwarfs in a star-forming region
text: A deep infrared survey of a young star-forming cloud identifies sixty brown dwarfs, objects too light to fuse hydrogen. Their mass function continues smoothly below the hydrogen burning limit, suggesting brown dwarfs form like stars from collapsing fragments of the molecular cloud rather than by ejection from multiple systems.

title: Gravitational lensing of a distant quasar
text: A foreground elliptical galaxy splits light from a background quasar into four images. Monitoring the images for three years measures time delays of up to ninety days between them. Combined with a lens mass model, the delays give an independent estimate of the Hubble constant that does not rely on the cosmic distance ladder.

title: Solar flares and coronal mass ejections
text: Extreme ultraviolet observations of the solar corona show that eruptive flares release magnetic energy stored in twisted flux ropes above active regions. Of the two hundred flares catalogued, those launching coronal mass ejections had larger magnetic helicity beforehand. Helicity may therefore help forecast which solar flares will drive geomagnetic storms at Earth.

title: The atmosphere of a hot exoplanet
text: Transmission spectroscopy of a hot Jupiter during transit detects water vapour absorption at 1.4 microns and a flat optical spectrum indicative of high-altitude clouds. Thermal emission measured at secondary eclipse shows a temperature inversion in the planet's upper atmosphere, likely caused by absorbing metal oxides heated by intense stellar irradiation.

title: Globular cluster ages from white dwarf cooling
text: Deep imaging of an old globular cluster reaches the faint end of its white dwarf cooling sequence. Because white dwarfs cool at a predictable rate, the luminosity of the faintest ones gives the cluster age, here twelve billion years, independent of main sequence turnoff fitting and its uncertainties in stellar convection and helium abundance.

title: A regulatory variant near a lactase gene
text: Lactase persistence into adulthood is associated with a single nucleotide variant thirteen kilobases upstream of the lactase gene. Reporter assays in intestinal cells show that the derived allele increases enhancer activity and transcription factor binding. Haplotype analysis indicates strong recent positive selection on this allele in populations with a history of dairying.

title: Genome-wide association study of height
text: A genome-wide association study of two hundred and fifty thousand individuals identifies seven hundred loci associated with adult height. Together the common variants explain about a quarter of the heritability. Associated genes are enriched for growth plate biology and skeletal development pathways, and many lie near regulatory elements active in chondrocytes.

title: CRISPR screens for essential genes
text: Pooled CRISPR knockout screens in twelve human cancer cell lines identify about two thousand genes required for proliferation. Guide RNAs targeting these genes are depleted after three weeks of culture. Most essential genes are shared across lines and encode ribosomal, splicing and DNA replication proteins, while a minority reflect lineage-specific dependencies.

title: Mitochondrial DNA heteroplasmy in families
text: Sequencing mitochondrial DNA from mothers and children across three hundred families shows that the fraction of mutant genomes, the heteroplasmy level, shifts sharply between generations. The pattern fits a bottleneck of a few dozen mitochondrial genomes during oogenesis, which explains why inherited mitochondrial disease varies so widely in severity among siblings.

title: Copy number variation and autism risk
text: De novo copy number variants were called from genotyping arrays in two thousand families with a child with autism. Large deletions and duplications arising de novo were four times more common in affected children than in unaffected siblings. Recurrent variants cluster at chromosome regions containing genes for synaptic proteins and chromatin remodelling.

title: Epigenetic clocks from DNA methylation
text: Methylation levels at three hundred and fifty CpG sites predict chronological age across many tissues with a median error of under four years. Individuals whose methylation age exceeds their calendar age show higher mortality in longitudinal cohorts, suggesting the epigenetic clock captures aspects of biological ageing beyond the passage of time.

title: Gene expression across human tissues
text: RNA sequencing of fifty tissues from nine hundred donors maps expression quantitative trait loci, genetic variants that change the transcription of nearby genes. Most genes have at least one such variant, and their effects are often shared across tissues. Colocalisation with disease association signals points to candidate causal genes at many risk loci.

title: Ancient DNA and population admixture
text: Genomes sequenced from two hundred ancient human skeletons spanning eight thousand years reveal successive waves of migration and admixture in Europe. Hunter-gatherer ancestry was largely replaced by early farmers from Anatolia, and later by steppe pastoralists. Allele frequency changes over time identify selection on pigmentation, diet and immune genes.

title: Recombination hotspots and PRDM9
text: Meiotic crossovers concentrate in narrow recombination hotspots across the genome. The zinc finger protein PRDM9 binds a degenerate DNA motif and marks hotspots by histone methylation. Alleles of PRDM9 with different zinc finger arrays activate different hotspot sets, explaining why recombination maps differ between populations and between closely related species.

title: Polygenic scores and their portability
text: Polygenic risk scores built from genome-wide association results in European ancestry samples predict coronary disease and type 2 diabetes less accurately in African and Asian ancestry cohorts. Differences in linkage disequilibrium and allele frequency between populations account for much of the loss, motivating more diverse genetic studies.

title: Single-cell transcriptomes of the developing kidney
text: Single-cell RNA sequencing of fetal kidney cells resolves nephron progenitors, ureteric bud and stromal lineages. Pseudotime analysis orders progenitors along a differentiation trajectory, and transcription factors switching on at branch points mark fate decisions. Several genes mutated in congenital kidney malformations are expressed in narrow progenitor populations.

title: Transposable elements as gene enhancers
text: Chromatin accessibility and histone marks show that endogenous retrovirus sequences act as enhancers in embryonic stem cells. Deleting one such element with CRISPR reduced expression of a neighbouring pluripotency gene by half. Transposable elements thus supply regulatory DNA that the host genome has co-opted to wire gene regulatory networks.

title: Mendelian randomisation of cholesterol
text: Using genetic variants in the HMGCR gene as instruments for lower LDL cholesterol, Mendelian randomisation estimates the causal effect of cholesterol on coronary heart disease free from confounding by lifestyle. The variants that mimic statin therapy also slightly raise type 2 diabetes risk, matching the side effect observed in randomised trials of statins.

title: Sex chromosome dosage compensation
text: In female mammals one X chromosome is silenced by the long noncoding RNA Xist, which coats the chromosome in cis and recruits repressive chromatin proteins. Allele-specific RNA sequencing finds that about fifteen percent of X-linked genes escape inactivation, and that escape genes vary between individuals and tissues.

title: Whole-genome sequencing in rare disease
text: Whole-genome sequencing of thirteen thousand patients with rare inherited disorders and their parents yielded a molecular diagnosis in a quarter of families. Diagnostic variants included structural rearrangements and noncoding mutations missed by exome sequencing. Pathogenic de novo mutations were most common in developmental disorders.

title: Measles outbreak and vaccination coverage
text: A measles outbreak of four hundred cases spread through school communities where vaccination coverage had fallen below ninety percent. Contact tracing estimated a reproduction number above twelve in unvaccinated clusters. Outbreak size across schools was strongly associated with the share of children with non-medical vaccine exemptions.

title: A cohort study of smoking and mortality
text: Following thirty-four thousand male physicians for fifty years, we find that men who smoked cigarettes throughout adult life died on average ten years earlier than lifelong non-smokers. Stopping smoking at age thirty avoided almost all of the excess risk, and stopping at fifty halved it. Lung cancer, vascular disease and respiratory disease accounted for most excess deaths.

title: Case-control study of a foodborne outbreak
text: An outbreak of Salmonella gastroenteritis affected two hundred people across four states. In a case-control study, cases were far more likely than controls to report eating raw sprouts in the week before illness, with an odds ratio of fourteen. Traceback identified a single seed lot, and whole-genome sequencing linked patient isolates to it.

title: Influenza seasonality and school terms
text: Weekly influenza-like illness reports from sentinel clinics over fifteen years show that transmission drops during school holidays and rebounds after children return. A transmission model fitted to surveillance data attributes about a fifth of the seasonal reduction in the reproduction number to school closures.

title: Randomised trial of a malaria vaccine
text: In a randomised controlled trial, eight thousand infants in malaria-endemic regions received a vaccine or a control injection. Over four years of follow-up the vaccine reduced clinical malaria episodes by thirty-six percent among children given a booster dose. Efficacy waned over time, and severe adverse events were balanced between arms.

title: Air pollution and cardiovascular hospital admissions
text: A time-series analysis of daily hospital admissions in twenty cities finds that each ten microgram increase in fine particulate matter is associated with a one percent rise in cardiovascular admissions the same day. Associations persisted after adjustment for temperature and influenza activity and were larger among adults over seventy-five.

title: Tuberculosis incidence and household contacts
text: Screening household contacts of patients with pulmonary tuberculosis found active disease in three percent and latent infection in half. Incidence among contacts was highest in the first year after the index diagnosis. Preventive therapy for infected children under five reduced subsequent disease by two thirds.

title: Hand hygiene and hospital infections
text: A stepped-wedge cluster trial introduced alcohol hand rub and audit feedback across sixteen hospital wards. Compliance with hand hygiene rose from forty to seventy percent, and hospital-acquired MRSA bloodstream infections fell by a third. Effects were sustained twelve months after the intervention ended on most wards.

title: Obesity prevalence in national surveys
text: Repeated cross-sectional health surveys with measured height and weight show adult obesity prevalence rising from fifteen to thirty-eight percent over four decades. Increases occurred in every age, sex and income group but were steepest among women with the lowest incomes. Prevalence in children doubled over the same period.

title: Cholera and contaminated water supply
text: Cholera deaths in one district were mapped by household and compared by water company. Households supplied with water drawn downstream of sewage outfalls had a cholera mortality eight times higher than those supplied from upstream sources. The natural experiment provides strong evidence that cholera spreads through contaminated drinking water.

title: Screening mammography and breast cancer mortality
text: In a cohort of women invited to biennial screening mammography from age fifty, breast cancer mortality was twenty percent lower than in a matched cohort not invited. Accounting for overdiagnosis, an estimated two hundred women need to be screened for twenty years to prevent one breast cancer death.

title: Antibiotic prescribing and resistance
text: Across European countries, outpatient antibiotic consumption correlates with the prevalence of penicillin-resistant pneumococci and macrolide resistance in community infections. Regions that reduced prescribing through public campaigns saw resistance decline after a lag of several years, supporting stewardship policies in primary care.

title: Seroprevalence survey after a pandemic wave
text: A household-based serosurvey of nine thousand residents after the first pandemic wave found antibodies in eleven percent of the population, ten times the number of confirmed cases. Seroprevalence was highest among essential workers and in crowded housing, and the infection fatality ratio was estimated at 0.8 percent, rising steeply with age.

title: Diet and colorectal cancer in a prospective cohort
text: In a prospective cohort of half a million adults, participants in the highest quintile of processed meat intake had an eighteen percent higher risk of colorectal cancer than those in the lowest, after adjusting for smoking, physical activity and body mass index. Dietary fibre intake was inversely associated with incidence.

title: Road traffic injury surveillance
text: Linking police crash reports with hospital records for five years shows that police data undercount serious injuries among cyclists by half. Injury incidence per kilometre travelled was highest for motorcyclists and young drivers. Areas that lowered urban speed limits to thirty kilometres per hour saw serious injuries fall by a quarter.

title: Contact tracing and the serial interval
text: Transmission pairs identified through contact tracing of a respiratory virus give a mean serial interval of five days, shorter than the incubation period, implying that much transmission occurs before symptoms appear. Isolating cases at symptom onset alone is therefore insufficient, and quarantine of traced contacts is needed to control spread.

title: Arctic sea ice decline and albedo feedback
text: Satellite passive microwave records show September Arctic sea ice extent declining by thirteen percent per decade since 1979. As bright ice gives way to dark open ocean, surface albedo falls and the ocean absorbs more solar radiation, amplifying warming. We estimate this albedo feedback accounts for a quarter of Arctic amplification in climate model simulations.

title: Ice cores and glacial carbon dioxide
text: Air bubbles trapped in Antarctic ice cores record atmospheric carbon dioxide over eight hundred thousand years. Concentrations swung between about 180 parts per million in glacial periods and 280 in interglacials, in step with Antarctic temperature. Present concentrations above 420 parts per million lie far outside this natural range.

title: Ocean heat content since 1955
text: Combining ship-based temperature profiles with the Argo float array, we estimate that the upper two thousand metres of the ocean have gained over three hundred zettajoules of heat since 1955. The ocean has absorbed about ninety percent of the excess energy trapped by greenhouse gases, and warming has penetrated deepest in the Southern Ocean.

title: Equilibrium climate sensitivity
text: We combine evidence from process understanding, the instrumental temperature record and palaeoclimate to constrain equilibrium climate sensitivity, the long-term warming from doubled carbon dioxide. The combined likely range is 2.6 to 3.9 degrees Celsius. Cloud feedbacks over subtropical oceans remain the largest source of uncertainty.

title: Sea level rise from ice sheet melt
text: Satellite gravimetry and altimetry show that the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets together lost about four hundred gigatonnes of ice per year over the last decade, contributing over a millimetre per year to global sea level rise. Thinning is fastest where warm ocean water reaches the grounding lines of marine-terminating glaciers.

title: El Nino and global temperature variability
text: Year-to-year swings in global mean surface temperature follow the El Nino Southern Oscillation with a lag of about three months. Removing the ENSO signal, volcanic aerosols and solar variability from the temperature record by regression leaves a steady warming trend of about 0.18 degrees per decade since 1979.

title: Attribution of an extreme heatwave
text: Using observations and large ensembles of climate model simulations with and without human greenhouse gas emissions, we find that a record summer heatwave would have been virtually impossible without anthropogenic warming. Such a heatwave has become at least one hundred and fifty times more likely and about two degrees hotter.

title: Permafrost thaw and carbon release
text: Northern permafrost soils store roughly twice as much carbon as the atmosphere. Borehole temperatures show permafrost warming at most monitoring sites. Incubation experiments and models indicate that thaw under high emissions could release one hundred gigatonnes of carbon as carbon dioxide and methane by 2100, an additional warming feedback.

title: Atlantic meridional overturning circulation
text: Mooring arrays across the subtropical Atlantic measure the meridional overturning circulation, which carries warm surface water north and returns cold deep water south. Transport weakened by about fifteen percent over the observing period. Climate models project further weakening as the North Atlantic freshens and warms.

title: Aerosols and cloud brightness
text: Ship tracks visible in satellite imagery show that aerosol particles from exhaust brighten marine stratocumulus clouds by increasing droplet number. Using a natural experiment from a change in shipping fuel sulphur regulations, we estimate the aerosol cloud radiative forcing and find that cleaner fuel has unmasked a small amount of greenhouse warming.

title: Precipitation extremes in a warmer atmosphere
text: Warmer air holds about seven percent more water vapour per degree of warming. Daily rainfall records from eight thousand stations show that heavy precipitation extremes have intensified at a rate close to this thermodynamic expectation across most land regions, while total annual precipitation changed little in many of them.

title: Tree rings and past drought
text: A network of tree-ring chronologies reconstructs summer soil moisture across western North America over twelve hundred years. Medieval megadroughts lasting decades exceeded anything in the instrumental record. The recent drought ranks among the most severe of the reconstruction, with warming temperatures contributing to its intensity.

title: Carbon budget for limiting warming
text: Global warming rises nearly linearly with cumulative carbon dioxide emissions. From this relation we estimate the remaining carbon budget for a fifty percent chance of limiting warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius at about two hundred and fifty gigatonnes of carbon dioxide from 2023, equivalent to six years of current emissions.

title: Mountain glacier mass balance
text: Repeat satellite elevation models of two hundred thousand mountain glaciers reveal accelerating thinning over two decades. Glaciers lost two hundred and sixty gigatonnes of ice per year, contributing a fifth of observed sea level rise. Loss was fastest in Alaska, the Andes and High Mountain Asia, threatening seasonal meltwater supply.

title: Ocean acidification and carbonate chemistry
text: Time series stations in the subtropical oceans record a steady decline in surface seawater pH of about 0.02 units per decade, as the ocean takes up anthropogenic carbon dioxide. Carbonate ion concentrations and aragonite saturation fall in step, which hampers calcification by corals, pteropods and other marine organisms.

title: Graphene transistors at room temperature
text: Single layers of graphene exfoliated onto silicon oxide show ambipolar field effect, with carrier mobility exceeding ten thousand square centimetres per volt second at room temperature. The absence of a band gap limits the on-off ratio of graphene transistors, motivating bilayer and nanoribbon structures in which a gap can be opened.

title: Perovskite solar cell stability
text: Metal halide perovskite solar cells reach power conversion efficiencies above twenty-five percent, but degrade under heat and humidity. Replacing methylammonium with a mix of formamidinium and caesium cations and adding a hydrophobic passivation layer kept efficiency above ninety percent of its initial value after a thousand hours of illumination at eighty-five degrees.

title: High-entropy alloys with fracture toughness
text: An equiatomic alloy of chromium, manganese, iron, cobalt and nickel forms a single face-centred cubic phase. Its fracture toughness and tensile strength increase as temperature falls to cryogenic levels, owing to nanoscale deformation twinning that adds strain hardening. The alloy rivals the best cryogenic steels.

title: Lithium-ion battery cathode degradation
text: Nickel-rich layered oxide cathodes offer high capacity but lose it over cycling. Electron microscopy of cycled particles shows intergranular cracking and a surface rock-salt phase that impedes lithium diffusion. A conformal coating and single-crystal particles reduced capacity fade to under ten percent after a thousand cycles.

title: Superconductivity in a hydride under pressure
text: Lanthanum hydride compressed to one hundred and seventy gigapascals in a diamond anvil cell shows zero electrical resistance below 250 kelvin. The superconducting transition shifts to lower temperature in a magnetic field, and its dependence on hydrogen isotope mass supports phonon-mediated pairing predicted by electronic structure calculations.

title: Self-healing polymers
text: A polymer network with reversible hydrogen bonds and dynamic disulphide crosslinks repairs cuts at room temperature. Cut samples pressed together for twenty-four hours recovered ninety percent of their original tensile strength. The healing rate depends on chain mobility, which we tune through the glass transition temperature of the polymer backbone.

title: Metal-organic frameworks for carbon capture
text: A metal-organic framework with open magnesium sites and amine-appended linkers adsorbs carbon dioxide from flue gas with a sharp step in its isotherm. The cooperative binding mechanism allows the framework to capture and release carbon dioxide with a small temperature swing, lowering the energy cost of regeneration compared with aqueous amine scrubbing.

title: Thermoelectric efficiency of tin selenide
text: Single crystals of tin selenide reach a thermoelectric figure of merit of 2.6 near 900 kelvin. The high performance arises from an ultralow lattice thermal conductivity caused by strongly anharmonic chemical bonding, which scatters phonons. Hole doping raises the electrical conductivity without sacrificing the Seebeck coefficient.

title: Additive manufacturing of titanium alloys
text: Laser powder bed fusion of titanium alloy produces columnar prior beta grains and a brittle martensitic microstructure. Adding a small amount of copper promotes fine equiaxed grains during solidification, and the printed alloy shows uniform tensile properties with higher strength than conventionally cast material.

title: Two-dimensional semiconductors beyond graphene
text: Monolayer molybdenum disulphide is a direct band gap semiconductor that emits light strongly, unlike its bulk crystal. Transistors made from monolayers achieve on-off current ratios above one hundred million. Strong spin-orbit coupling splits the valence band and enables valley-selective optical excitation with circularly polarised light.

title: Corrosion resistance of stainless steels
text: Pitting corrosion of austenitic stainless steels initiates at manganese sulphide inclusions where the passive chromium oxide film is thin. Electrochemical measurements show that steels with higher molybdenum and nitrogen content repassivate faster. Laser surface melting dissolves the inclusions and raises the pitting potential in chloride solutions.

title: Quantum dots for light emission
text: Colloidal cadmium-free indium phosphide quantum dots with a zinc selenide and zinc sulphide shell reach photoluminescence quantum yields near one hundred percent. The emission colour is set by the nanocrystal size through quantum confinement. Electroluminescent devices built from the dots show external quantum efficiency above twenty percent.

title: Glass transition in metallic glasses
text: Rapid cooling of a zirconium-based alloy melt suppresses crystallisation and forms a bulk metallic glass. Calorimetry shows a wide supercooled liquid region, which allows the glass to be thermoplastically moulded like a polymer. The amorphous structure gives high strength and elastic limit but limited ductility owing to shear band localisation.

title: Ceramic thermal barrier coatings
text: Yttria-stabilised zirconia coatings protect turbine blades from combustion gases. At temperatures above 1200 degrees Celsius the coating sinters and loses strain tolerance. Rare-earth zirconate pyrochlores have lower thermal conductivity and phase stability at high temperature but lower fracture toughness, so bilayer coatings combine the two ceramics.

title: Topological insulator surface states
text: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of bismuth selenide crystals reveals a single Dirac cone of surface states inside the bulk band gap. Spin-resolved measurements show the electron spin locked perpendicular to its momentum, protecting surface conduction from backscattering by nonmagnetic impurities, as predicted for a three-dimensional topological insulator.

title: Place cells and grid cells in navigation
text: Recording neurons in the rat hippocampus and entorhinal cortex during foraging shows that place cells fire at specific locations, while grid cells fire at the vertices of a triangular lattice tiling the environment. Grid spacing increases along the dorsoventral axis, and together these neurons form a spatial map supporting navigation and memory.

title: Dopamine neurons and reward prediction error
text: Midbrain dopamine neurons in monkeys fire a burst to an unexpected juice reward. After learning, the burst moves to a cue predicting reward, and firing pauses when an expected reward is omitted. This pattern matches the reward prediction error of temporal difference learning, linking dopamine signalling to reinforcement learning.

title: Optogenetic control of neural circuits
text: Expressing the light-gated ion channel channelrhodopsin in genetically defined neurons allows millisecond control of their spiking with blue light. Activating these neurons in the mouse amygdala elicited freezing, and silencing them with halorhodopsin blocked fear conditioning, establishing a causal role for this circuit in learned fear behaviour.

title: Synaptic plasticity and long-term potentiation
text: High-frequency stimulation of hippocampal synapses produces long-term potentiation, a lasting increase in synaptic strength. Induction requires calcium influx through NMDA receptors when presynaptic glutamate release coincides with postsynaptic depolarisation. Blocking NMDA receptors impairs spatial learning, supporting LTP as a cellular basis of memory.

title: Functional MRI of face perception
text: Functional magnetic resonance imaging of human volunteers viewing faces, objects and scenes identifies a region of the fusiform gyrus that responds more strongly to faces than to any other category. The response is reduced for inverted faces, and patients with lesions near this cortical region show prosopagnosia, an inability to recognise faces.

title: Sleep and memory consolidation
text: During slow-wave sleep, hippocampal place cells replay sequences of activity experienced during the day, coordinated with cortical spindles and slow oscillations. Disrupting these sharp wave ripples after training impaired spatial memory in rats, indicating that sleep replay helps consolidate memories in cortical networks.

title: Amyloid and tau in Alzheimer's disease
text: Positron emission tomography in older adults shows that amyloid plaques accumulate in the cortex years before cognitive symptoms. Tau tangles spread from the entorhinal cortex to association cortex in a stereotyped sequence, and tau burden, more than amyloid, correlates with neuronal loss and cognitive decline in Alzheimer's disease.

title: Orientation tuning in visual cortex
text: Microelectrode recordings from the primary visual cortex of the cat show neurons that respond selectively to bars of light at a particular orientation. Simple cells respond to a bar at a precise position, complex cells across a range of positions. Neurons with similar orientation preference are arranged in columns across the cortex.

title: Brain-computer interface for typing
text: Microelectrode arrays implanted in the motor cortex of a person with paralysis recorded neural activity while she attempted handwriting. A recurrent neural network decoded the activity into letters at ninety characters per minute with over ninety percent accuracy, demonstrating a high-performance brain-computer interface for communication.

title: Adult neurogenesis in the hippocampus
text: Labelling dividing cells with thymidine analogues shows that new neurons are born in the dentate gyrus of adult rodents and integrate into hippocampal circuits. Running and enriched environments increase neurogenesis, while stress reduces it. Blocking neurogenesis impairs discrimination between similar contexts, a function called pattern separation.

title: Connectome of the fly brain
text: Electron microscopy of an entire adult fruit fly brain, reconstructed with automated segmentation and proofreading, maps one hundred and forty thousand neurons and fifty million synapses. The connectome reveals the wiring of the central complex, which supports navigation, and the mushroom body circuits for olfactory learning.

title: Ion channels and the action potential
text: Voltage clamp experiments on the squid giant axon separate the membrane current into sodium and potassium components. A model with voltage-dependent conductances for each ion reproduces the shape and propagation of the action potential, and the threshold and refractory period of the nerve impulse emerge from channel gating kinetics.

title: Motor cortex population dynamics
text: Recording hundreds of neurons in monkey motor cortex during reaching reveals that population activity rotates through a low-dimensional state space. Preparatory activity before movement sets the initial state of these dynamics, which then unfold to generate muscle commands. Single-neuron tuning to reach direction emerges from the population dynamics.

title: Microglia prune synapses in development
text: Microglia, the immune cells of the brain, engulf synaptic material in the developing visual thalamus. Synapses tagged by complement proteins are preferentially eliminated, and mice lacking the complement receptor retain excess synapses. Activity-dependent synaptic pruning by microglia thus refines neural circuits during development.

title: Deep brain stimulation for Parkinson's disease
text: High-frequency electrical stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus through implanted electrodes reduces tremor, rigidity and slowness of movement in Parkinson's disease. Local field potential recordings show exaggerated beta oscillations in the basal ganglia that are suppressed by stimulation, guiding adaptive closed-loop deep brain stimulation.
